The worker container crashed at about 22:00 UTC (agent API error, not a code error); every process died. Restarted at 23:40 UTC (elapsed 5.9 h) with ONE orchestrator (q32, q14; q8 was complete) and ONE evaluator, both behind exclusive lock files. New-request stop moved to elapsed 7.5 h and the SEL-W quality cutoff to 8.6 h because the time base shifted by about 1.7 h.

From 21:21 to 22:00 UTC two orchestrators ran at once (the kill hit a shell wrapper, its Python child survived). Effects: 5 duplicate q32 BASE rows (slots 43, 45, 46, 48, 49) moved to data/samples_raw_q32_duplicates_crash_era.jsonl, keeping the first row per slot (the one the evaluator scored); the naming files of q14/q32 mixed empty 96-token replies with genuine ones, so a clean rerun goes to data/naming_raw_<m>_clean.jsonl and COMMIT #3; the payload files of commit2_q14 and commit2_q32 were overwritten after their hashes were logged, so lines 2-3 of commitments.log no longer match the files on disk. B_1..B_5 are identical (BF, FF, WF, AWF, LF) in every version, so NAME/HOLD cells are unaffected.
OpenRouter concurrency 16 (was 12) after the crash, so that the never-drop set, HOLD_5 and the INSTR cells fit before the moved stop time.
After the restart the container has a 10.2-CPU cgroup quota (was 7.65), so the evaluator runs 8 workers instead of 5. CPU-time limits are per process, so the results do not change.
